Grabow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Grabów, Poland

Not demolished. Grabów, granted town rights in 1372 and downgraded in 1870, recorded its first Jews in 1764, initially under Łęczyca's religious jurisdiction; population reached 45.6% (146) by 1800, nearly half the town (915) by 1921. In April 1942, all of Grabów's Jews were transported to the Chełmno extermination camp. This cemetery, most likely established in the 19th century, is completely destroyed with no surviving matzevot; former District Museum director Łucja Nowak led efforts to erect a stone obelisk with informational plaque at the site.
